items.question: What operations is the helicopter approved for?
items.explanation: The B3e flight manual states the helicopter is approved for day and night VFR operations.

items.question: Aerobatic maneuvers are:
items.explanation: Section 2.1 explicitly states that aerobatic maneuvers are forbidden.

items.question: Engine start is prohibited:
options: When snow or ice has collected in or around the engine air intake
items.explanation: Engine start is prohibited if snow or ice has accumulated in or around the engine air intake.

items.question: Flight in freezing rain or icing conditions (visible moisture with temperature that can produce ice) is:
items.explanation: Section 2.1 forbids flight in freezing rain or icing conditions (visible moisture with temperature conducive to producing ice).

items.question: Intentional engine power reduction in flight using the twist grip is:
items.explanation: Intentional power reduction in flight with the twist grip is prohibited except during engine failure training or specified emergency procedures.

items.question: What is the minimum crew?
options: One pilot in the left seat
One pilot in the right seat
items.explanation: Minimum crew is one pilot in the right seat.

items.question: What is the maximum number of persons on board, including flight crew?
items.explanation: The maximum number of persons on board, including flight crew, is six.

items.question: On the VEMD, what does a red underlining of a parameter value indicate?
options: At or above a safety limit or maximum takeoff power
items.explanation: Section 2.1 states that numerical values are underlined in red when at or above a safety limit or maximum takeoff power. The red underlining flashes to attract attention.

items.question: On the VEMD, what does a yellow underlining of a parameter value indicate?
items.explanation: Section 2.1 states that numerical values are underlined in yellow when the parameter is in the caution or takeoff power range.

items.question: What does flashing red underlining of a parameter value on the VEMD indicate?
options: That the parameter is at or above a safety limit and the system is drawing pilot attention
items.explanation: To attract attention, the B3e manual specifies that red underlining flashes when a parameter is at or above a safety limit or maximum takeoff power.

items.question: What is the maximum internal weight for flight, takeoff and landing?
items.explanation: Section 2.2 gives 2250 kg (4961 lb). 2370 kg (5225 lb) applies only with the SUP.28 increased-weight option (high landing gear and dual hydraulics).

items.question: What is the forward longitudinal CG limit at the maximum internal weight of 2250 kg?
items.explanation: Section 2.2 Figure 1: at 2250 kg the CG envelope runs from 3.21 m (forward limit) to 3.425 m (rearward limit). The datum is 3.40 m (133.8 in) forward of the main rotor head center line.

items.question: What is the rearward longitudinal CG limit at the maximum internal weight of 2250 kg?
items.explanation: Section 2.2 Figure 1: at 2250 kg the rearward limit is 3.425 m. The limit moves aft as weight decreases, reaching 3.498 m at the minimum weight.

items.question: What is the maximum left lateral CG?
items.explanation: Section 2.2: maximum left CG is 0.18 m (7.08 in) and maximum right CG is 0.14 m (5.51 in), measured from the plane of symmetry.

items.question: What is the lower limit of the NR normal operating range with power on?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Main Rotor Limitations: 320–375 rpm is the lower caution range; the normal operating range is 375–405 rpm.

items.question: What is the upper limit of the NR normal operating range?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Main Rotor Limitations: the normal operating range is 375–405 rpm; 405–430 rpm is the upper caution range.

items.question: Which NR range is the upper caution range?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Main Rotor Limitations: 405–430 rpm is the upper caution range. 430 rpm is the maximum power-off NR.

items.question: What is the power-off minimum rotor speed (Nr)?
items.explanation: Power-off minimum Nr is 320 rpm.

items.question: What is the power-off maximum rotor speed (Nr)?
items.explanation: Power-off maximum Nr is 430 rpm.

items.question: What is the N2 (power turbine) normal operating range?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Engine Limitations: N2 minimum is 367 rpm, the normal operating range is 367–413 rpm and 413 rpm is the maximum continuous. NR 386 rpm corresponds to N2 39158 rpm.

items.question: What is the maximum transient N2 limit?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Engine Limitations: maximum transient N2 is 440 rpm (20 sec).

items.question: What is the minimum stabilized N1 speed?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Engine Limitations: minimum stabilized N1 is 67 %. 100 % N1 corresponds to 52110 rpm.

items.question: What is the maximum continuous N1 rating on the ΔN1 scale?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Engine Limitations: maximum continuous ΔN1 = -4 %; takeoff power ΔN1 = -4 % to 0 %; maximum takeoff rating ΔN1 = 0 %; maximum transient ΔN1 = +1 % (20 sec or less).

items.question: What is the maximum continuous TOT in flight?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 TOT limitations (flight): maximum continuous rating 905 °C; takeoff power 905–949 °C.

items.question: What is the maximum takeoff rating TOT in flight?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 TOT limitations (flight): maximum takeoff rating is 949 °C (takeoff power range 905–949 °C).

items.question: What is the maximum transient TOT in flight?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 TOT limitations (flight): maximum transient is 981 °C (20 sec).

items.question: What is the maximum transient TOT during start?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 TOT limitations (starting): maximum transient 840 °C (10 sec); maximum continuous 750 °C.

items.question: Wide-cut Jet B (JP-4) may be used as a replacement fuel only within which envelope?
items.explanation: Section 2.5: Jet A-1, Jet A, JP-8 and JP-5 are normal fuels. Wide-cut Jet B / JP-4 is a replacement fuel limited to OAT ≤ 25 °C and Hp ≤ 5000 ft (1524 m); TS-1 / RT kerosene to OAT ≤ 40 °C and Hp ≤ 15 000 ft (4572 m).

items.question: What is the maximum engine oil temperature?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Oil Temperature Limitations: the maximum temperature is 117 °C; the caution range is shown on the gauge.

items.question: With 3 to 3.9 cSt engine oil, what is the minimum oil temperature before power application?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Oil Temperature Limitations: -10 °C for 3 to 3.9 cSt oil (0 °C for 5 cSt oil). During warm-up keep the collective in full low pitch; the twist grip can be in IDLE or FLIGHT.

items.question: On which engine parameter do the oil pressure limits depend?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Oil Pressure Limitations: oil pressure has variable limits that depend on N1.

items.question: What is the maximum operating altitude in flight for the basic B3e?
items.explanation: Section 2.3: Hp = 23 000 ft (7010 m). Post MOD 07-3368 the limit is Hp = 20 000 ft (6096 m).

items.question: Post MOD 07-3368, what is the maximum operating altitude in flight?
items.explanation: Section 2.3 (conditional revision): post MOD 07-3368 Hp = 20 000 ft (6096 m). The basic limit is 23 000 ft (7010 m).

items.question: What is the minimum temperature limit for the flight envelope?
items.explanation: Section 2.3: minimum temperature -40 °C. For cold weather operations refer to SUP.4.

items.question: What is the maximum temperature limit for the flight envelope?
items.explanation: Section 2.3: maximum temperature ISA+35 °C, limited to +50 °C.

items.question: What is the maximum slope for landing and rotor stopping (nose up)?
items.explanation: Section 2.3: nose up 10°, nose down 6°, sideways 8°.

items.question: What is the maximum slope for landing (nose-down)?
items.explanation: Maximum slope for nose-down landing is 6°.

items.question: What is the maximum slope for landing (side slope)?
items.explanation: Maximum side slope for landing is 8°.

items.question: What battery voltage does the pre-start check require?
items.explanation: Section 4.3 engine pre-start check: VEMD check includes battery voltage > 22 V.

items.question: What is the maximum voltage in the electrical circuit limitations?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Electrical Circuit Limitations: maximum voltage 31.5 V (rated voltage 26–29 V).

items.question: What is the maximum continuous current with the standard starter generator?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Electrical Circuit Limitations: 150 A maximum continuous. An optional 200 A starter generator (SUP.29) replaces the basic unit.

items.question: In-flight intentional VEMD complete cut-off (lane 1 and 2 together) is:
items.explanation: Section 2.1 lists in-flight intentional VEMD complete cut-off (lane 1 + 2) among the forbidden operations, alongside aerobatics and in-flight power reduction via the twist grip outside training/emergency use.

items.question: Flight in falling snow without the optional sand filter installed is:
items.explanation: Section 2.1 forbids flight in falling snow unless the optional sand filter is installed — a separate restriction from the icing/freezing rain prohibition.

items.question: What is the minimum internal weight for flight, takeoff and landing?
items.explanation: Section 2.2 gives the minimum internal weight for flight, takeoff and landing as 1310 kg (2888 lb).

items.question: With doors closed and OAT below -30 °C, how must the calculated power-on VNE be adjusted?
items.explanation: Section 2.3 requires the calculated power-on VNE to be reduced by 10 kt (18.5 km/h) when OAT is below -30 °C, with doors closed.

items.question: With doors closed and OAT below -20 °C, how must the calculated power-off VNE be adjusted?
options: Reduced by 20 kt, with a minimum of 65 kt
items.explanation: Section 2.3 requires the calculated power-off VNE to be reduced by 20 kt (37 km/h) when OAT is below -20 °C, down to a minimum of 65 kt (120 km/h).

items.question: Excluding emergencies and failures, what is the maximum speed for a running landing?
items.explanation: Section 2.3 limits running landings (excluding emergencies and failures) to a maximum speed of 40 kt (74 km/h).

items.question: When is it prohibited to use the rotor brake?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Main Rotor Limitations prohibits using the rotor brake prior to engine shutdown.

items.question: What is the minimum time required between two consecutive rotor brake applications?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 requires a minimum of 5 minutes between two consecutive rotor brake applications.

items.question: Takeoff power use is limited to a maximum airspeed of:
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Takeoff Power limits use of takeoff power to a maximum airspeed of 40 KIAS.

items.question: On this helicopter, 100% torque (TRQ) corresponds to:
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Main Transmission Limitations notes that 100% torque corresponds to 535 kW at NR 386 rpm.

items.question: Using 5 cSt engine oil, what is the minimum oil temperature before power application?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Oil Temperature Limitations sets the minimum oil temperature before power application at 0 °C for 5 cSt oil (or -10 °C for 3 to 3.9 cSt oil).

items.question: What is the maximum load permitted in the RH cargo compartment?
items.explanation: Section 2.5 Baggage Compartment Load Limitations sets the RH cargo compartment maximum at 100 kg (220 lb), with a maximum distributed load of 300 kg/m².

items.question: What is the maximum load permitted in the LH cargo compartment?
items.explanation: Section 2.5 Baggage Compartment Load Limitations sets the LH cargo compartment maximum at 120 kg (264 lb).

items.question: What is the maximum load permitted on the rear cabin floor?
items.explanation: Section 2.5 Cabin Compartment Load Limitations sets the rear cabin floor maximum at 310 kg (682 lb), with a maximum distributed load of 300 kg/m².

items.question: After a second failed engine start attempt, how long must the starter cool before a further attempt?
items.explanation: Section 2.5 Engine Starter/Generator limits give a 30-minute cooling period after a second failed start attempt, versus 1 minute cooling between the first two attempts.

items.question: What is the minimum number of radio/audio headsets required on board?
items.explanation: Section 2.5 Mandatory Equipment requires at least two adequate radio/audio headsets on board — one worn by the pilot to monitor ICS audio warnings, plus a spare.

items.question: Continued flight operation in servo-transparency (load feedback felt in the controls) is:
items.explanation: Section 2.3 Maneuvering Limitations prohibits continued operation in servo-transparency, warning that the phenomenon can be hazardous at low clearance from the ground, particularly in a right turn.

items.question: On T-PED tolerant aircraft, where must transmitting portable electronic devices have their radio transmission inhibited?
items.explanation: Section 2.5 states that on T-PED tolerant aircraft, use is permitted without restriction except in the rear cargo hold, where any T-PED must be turned off and radio transmission inhibited.

items.question: What is the VNE power on at Hp = 0 (doors closed)?
items.explanation: Section 2.3 airspeed limits: VNE power on is 155 kt (287 km/h) at Hp = 0, less 3 kt per 1000 ft.

items.question: What is the VNE power off at Hp = 0 (doors closed)?
items.explanation: Section 2.3 airspeed limits: VNE power off is 125 kt (232 km/h) at Hp = 0, less 3 kt per 1000 ft.

items.question: By how much does VNE decrease per 1000 ft of altitude (doors closed)?
items.explanation: Section 2.3 airspeed limits: both VNE power on and VNE power off are reduced by 3 kt per 1000 ft (5.5 km/h per 300 m).

items.question: At what NR does the low rotor speed aural warning sound?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Main Rotor Limitations: low NR aural warning at or below 360 rpm.

items.question: At what NR does the high rotor speed aural warning sound?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Main Rotor Limitations: high NR aural warning at or above 410 rpm.

items.question: What is the maximum NR at which the rotor brake may be applied?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Main Rotor Limitations: rotor brake operation maximum speed is 170 rpm.

items.question: What is the maximum continuous torque rating?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Main Transmission Limitations: 92.7 % maximum continuous; 92.7–100 % takeoff power.

items.question: What is the maximum takeoff rating torque?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Main Transmission Limitations: maximum takeoff rating 100 %.

items.question: What is the maximum transient torque, and for how long?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Main Transmission Limitations: maximum transient 104 % (5 sec).

items.question: What is the maximum continuous rating on the First Limitation Indicator (FLI)?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 First Limitation Indicator: 9.6 maximum continuous rating; 9.6–10 takeoff power; 10 maximum takeoff rating; 10.4 maximum transient (5 sec).

items.question: What is the maximum transient rating on the FLI?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 First Limitation Indicator: maximum transient rating 10.4 (5 sec).

items.question: Post OP-4309, how long may N1 and/or TOT be in the takeoff power range?
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Takeoff Power: if N1 and/or TOT is in the takeoff power range, use is limited to 5 min continuous pre-OP-4309 and 30 min continuous post-OP-4309.

items.question: If only torque (TRQ) is in the takeoff power range, the time limit is:
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Takeoff Power: if only torque is in the takeoff power range there is no time limit.

items.question: Use of heating and demisting is authorised up to:
items.explanation: Section 2.4 Takeoff Power: use of heating and demisting is authorised up to maximum TOP (takeoff power).

items.question: What is the maximum load in the rear cargo compartment?
items.explanation: Section 2.5 Baggage Compartment Load Limitations: rear cargo compartment 80 kg (176 lb) at a maximum distributed load of 145 kg/m².

items.question: What is the maximum load on the forward left cabin floor?
items.explanation: Section 2.5 Cabin Compartment Load Limitations: forward left cabin floor 150 kg (330 lb); rear cabin floor 310 kg (682 lb).

items.question: With SUP.28 (high landing gear and dual hydraulics), what is the maximum internal weight in flight?
items.explanation: SUP.28 Limitations: maximum internal weight in flight and for IGE takeoff and landing is 2370 kg (5225 lb).
